3-ON-2 DRIVE AND KICK, PAINT TOUCH SCORE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will start in 5-out spacings. Two defenders will play defense. The offense will stay on for three repetitions in a row (we will call these bursts). The defense will throw the ball to any offensive player to begin the burst. The offense will then play 3-on-2, only being able to score a rim finish or a catch-and-shoot 3PT shot. However, the offense can only shoot after a player penetrates and achieves a paint touch. The defense can steal the ball before the paint touch has been achieved.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Must get two paint touches instead.
- Space using the weakside dunker at all times.
- Add a third defender and play 3-on-3.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players begin from different 5-out spacings.
- Remind players to stay for 3 bursts.
- Ensure players get the paint touch(es).

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How else could you achieve the paint touch?
- Did the help defender commit to stopping you?

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 LINE START

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Begin with an offensive player holding a ball and under the basket, facing the 3PT line. A defender will stand behind them, followed by another offensive player, another defender, another offensive player, and another defender (alternating offense and defense). The offensive and defenders will start in a straight line under the basket. As the ball-handler dribbles to a 5-out spacing spot, the other two offensive teammates must also go to suitable spacing spots outside of the lava. The moment the offensive handler gets outside the 3PT line, a live 3-on-3 starts. Play until a score, with the defense clearing the ball on each possession change and then scoring through any means possible.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Spacing and advantage

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Turnover is called if players catch inside unless they are completing some type of non-scripted cutting action.
- After the first score, the defense has to inbound the ball and get the ball to the half-court line to score a touchdown within eight seconds. If they do this, they get the opportunity to transition back to score points. If the offense steals the ball, they get the chance to score the points.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Encourage players to use triggers to create advantages (e.g. post ups, 1-on-1 with good spacing, get/pick actions, etc.).

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you create an advantage?
- Defensively, how can you recover to neutral if the offense creates an advantage?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I BLIND SHOOTING

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner and a ball. Three groups can play 1-on-1 on the same basket at the same time. The defender will start blind to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender back. As soon as they lift the ball from the defense back, it becomes a live 1-on-1. The offense has a maximum of three dribbles to score but can only score by shooting outside the paint. Each repetition should have a different starting location.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense is not allowed to block the shooter, but can distract them to try and miss.
- The offense and defense must change partners after they both play offense.
- The offense can only score with one dribble.
- The offense gets double points for a swish.
- The offense begins in the paint, facing away from the basket, and must get out to space and shoot within three dribbles.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help the players read the playing space and successfully organize themselves by communicating whose turn it is.
- Challenge players to get their shot off quickly before the defender can recover.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Attempting to shoot as controlled as possible
- Exploring different ways to stop (e.g. jump stop, stride stop, etc).

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you use the space before the defender can recover?
- How can the defender rear view contest without fouling?

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, the losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY WORDS

- How can you get the most efficient shot?
- How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?
- What can you do to space the floor effectively?

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Pass and cut is a turnover: create an advantage through static 1-on-1.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.
